testDefinitions.displayName: Identification (reactions of zinc)
testDefinitions.notes: Reactions of zinc per USP <191>: 100 mg/mL solution gives white precipitate with H2S in presence of sodium acetate (insoluble in acetic acid, dissolved by 3 N HCl); white precipitate with ammonium sulfide TS; white precipitate with potassium ferrocyanide TS insoluble in 3 N HCl.

sources.source: Zinc Gluconate__STM Calcium  Zinc Gluconate.txt:30

testDefinitions.displayName: Identification (TLC, gluconate)
testDefinitions.notes: TLC identification per USP <621>: 0.25 mm silica gel layer; 5 µL application of 10 mg/mL sample vs 10 mg/mL USP Potassium Gluconate RS; developing solvent alcohol:ethyl acetate:ammonium hydroxide:water (50:10:10:30); spray reagent 2.5 g ammonium molybdate + 1.0 g ceric sulfate in 2 N sulfuric acid; principal spot corresponds in colour and size.

sources.source: Zinc Gluconate__STM Calcium  Zinc Gluconate.txt:30

testDefinitions.displayName: Arsenic (limit test, arsenic apparatus)
testDefinitions.notes: Arsenic limit test per USP <211> procedure 1: 1 g sample vs 3.0 mL standard arsenic solution (1 µg/mL = 3 ppm) in 35 mL water with 20 mL 7 N sulfuric acid, KI TS, stannous chloride TS, isopropanol; generate arsine with granular zinc into silver diethyldithiocarbamate TS. Test colour must not exceed standard.

sources.source: Zinc Gluconate__STM Calcium  Zinc Gluconate.txt:33

testDefinitions.displayName: Lead (limit test by AAS)
testDefinitions.notes: Lead limit test by AAS per USP <852>: 1.0 g sample extracted with 9 N HCl, ascorbic acid-NaI and trioctylphosphine oxide into organic layer; standard 2 µg/mL Pb organic layer; air-acetylene flame at 283.3 nm. Sample absorbance must not exceed standard absorbance (NMT 10 ppm).

sources.source: Zinc Gluconate__STM Calcium  Zinc Gluconate.txt:34

testDefinitions.displayName: Reducing substances in zinc gluconate (residual titration)
testDefinitions.notes: Residual titration per USP <541>: 1.0 g sample in 10 mL water + 25 mL alkaline cupric citrate TS, boil 5 min, cool, add 25 mL 0.6 N acetic acid, 10.0 mL 0.1 N iodine VS, 10 mL 3 N HCl; titrate excess iodine with 0.1 N sodium thiosulfate VS using starch TS. Blank with 10 mL water. Result % (as dextrose) = [(VB - VS) * N * F / W] * 100, F = 27 mg/mEq.

sources.source: Zinc Gluconate__STM Calcium  Zinc Gluconate.txt:36

testDefinitions.displayName: Assay of zinc gluconate (complexometric titration)
testDefinitions.notes: Direct complexometric titration per USP <541>: 700 mg sample in 100 mL water + 5 mL ammonia-ammonium chloride buffer TS + 0.1 mL Eriochrome black TS, titrated with 0.05 M edetate disodium VS to deep blue; blank with 100 mL water. Result % on anhydrous basis (uses Karl Fischer water result RM-KF). Titrant defined in g03.

sources.source: Zinc Gluconate__STM Calcium  Zinc Gluconate.txt:39

testDefinitions.displayName: HCl insoluble matter in tartrazine lake
testDefinitions.notes: 5.0 g sample + 10 mL HCl + 50 mL water, filter through weighed paper, dry at 100-105 °C to constant weight. Formula as written in the STM has inconsistent labels [% = (W3 - W1) / W2 x 100]; per Rule 6 and README decision, Measurement test where analyst enters the final %.

testDefinitions.displayName: Acidity (Ferric ammonium citrate green)
testDefinitions.notes: Acidity per USP 2024: dissolve 1 g in 100 mL water; test with calibrated pH meter; solution must show acidic medium.

sources.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green.txt:32

testDefinitions.displayName: Identification by ignition (Ferric ammonium citrate green)
testDefinitions.notes: Identification test A per USP 2024: ignite about 0.5 g sample; chars and leaves residue of iron oxide.

sources.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green.txt:30

testDefinitions.displayName: Identification with ammonium hydroxide (Ferric ammonium citrate green)
testDefinitions.notes: Identification test B per USP 2024: 10 mL of 1 in 100 solution + 6 N ammonium hydroxide dropwise; solution darkens, no precipitate forms.

sources.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green.txt:30

testDefinitions.displayName: Identification with potassium permanganate (Ferric ammonium citrate green)
testDefinitions.notes: Identification test C per USP 2024: 5 mL of 1 in 100 solution + 0.3 mL potassium permanganate TS + 4 mL mercuric sulphate TS; heat to boiling; white precipitate forms.

sources.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green.txt:30

testDefinitions.displayName: Assay of ferric ammonium citrate (iodometric titration)
testDefinitions.titrationEquivalencyFactorDerivation: 5.585 mg Fe per mL of 0.1 N Na2S2O3 / 0.1 = 55.85 mg/mEq
testDefinitions.notes: Iodometric titration per USP: about 1 g sample in 25 mL water + 5 mL HCl + 4 g KI, stand 15 min protected from light; add 100 mL water, titrate liberated iodine with 0.1 N sodium thiosulfate VS using starch TS; blank determination. 1 mL of 0.1 N thiosulfate = 5.585 mg Fe. Shared procedure between STM-RM-001 (green) and STM-RM-048 (brown).

testDefinitions.displayName: Identification of silicate (Colloidal anhydrous silica)
testDefinitions.notes: Reaction of silicate per BP 2025: 20 mg sample + 10 mg NaF + few drops sulfuric acid R in platinum crucible; cover with plastic plate carrying suspended water drop; warm gently. White ring forms rapidly around the drop of water.

sources.source: Colloidal Anhydrous Silica__New_New.txt:32

testDefinitions.displayName: Loss on ignition (Colloidal anhydrous silica)
testDefinitions.notes: Loss on ignition per BP 2025: 0.2 g sample in dry crucible ignited at 900 ± 50 °C for 2 h, cool in desiccator, weigh. Limit NMT 5.0%.

testDefinitions.displayName: Assay of SiO2 (Colloidal anhydrous silica)
testDefinitions.notes: Decision per Rule 6 and README: multi-step HF volatilization from the loss-on-ignition residue cannot be calculated by standard gravimetric workflow; Measurement test, analyst enters the final % SiO2 (ignited substance).

solutions.name: 0.1 N Sodium thiosulfate VS
solutions.instructions: Dissolve about 26 g of sodium thiosulfate and 200 mg of sodium carbonate in 1000 mL of recently boiled and cooled water.
solutions.notes: Standardization per STM-RM-001 line 26: accurately weigh about 210 mg of primary standard potassium dichromate, previously pulverized and dried, dissolve in 100 mL water in 500-mL glass-stoppered flask; add 3 g KI, 2 g NaHCO3, 5 mL HCl, stand 10 min in the dark, titrate liberated iodine with thiosulfate using 3 mL starch TS; blank determination. Equivalence: 49.037 * 0.1 = 4.904 mg K2Cr2O7 / mL thiosulfate. House defaults applied.

solutions.name: 0.1 N Iodine VS
solutions.instructions: Dissolve about 14 g of iodine in a solution of 36 g of potassium iodide in 100 mL of water, add 3 drops of hydrochloric acid, and dilute with water to 1000.0 mL.
solutions.notes: Standardization per STM-RM-050 line 26: 25.0 mL iodine solution + 100 mL water + 1 mL 1 N HCl, titrate with 0.1 N sodium thiosulfate VS until pale yellow, add 2 mL starch TS, continue to colorless. House defaults applied.
